newsitem.title: MEXICO: Analysts forecast Carso Q2 lower.
newsitem.headline: Analysts forecast Carso Q2 lower.

text.p: Analysts predicted Mexican holding company Grupo Carso's recent acquisitions would boost its second quarter sales, but the newcomers' low margins would undermine operating and net earnings.
Three analysts surveyed by Reuters forecast average sales of 7.039 billion pesos for the second quarter, a real increase of 10.1 percent from the same quarter in 1996.
Net earnings were meanwhile predicted at an average of 558 million pesos, equivalent to 0.68 pesos per share -- a drop of 24.1 percent in real year-on-year terms.
Goldman Sachs analyst Kerry McHugh, however, said net earnings comparisons were distorted by local accountancy practices.
"Below the operating line, the net earnings don't mean mean much," she said.

The analysts said the picture was better for average operating earnings which fell less than net earnings. Average operating earnings slipped 11.4 percent from year-ago numbers to 1.150 billion pesos.
But they also said that comparisons were fraught by a change in Carso's lineup since last year.

"In year-on-year terms, it is an apples-and-oranges comparison," said Fred Searby, an analyst with Societe Generale. "Nonetheless, we expect a sequential improvement from the first quarter," he added.
Carso bought an estimated 82 percent of troubled retailer Sears Roebuck de Mexico from Sears Roebuck Co during the second quarter.
The group's cable-making division, Condumex, meanwhile acquired rival Latincasa.
Analysts said Latincasa had recently posted low margins and Sears had actually posted losses, so their incorporation into the overall balance sheet would hurt operating margins.
"Investors understand Carso will try to turn Sears around," Alexander Ryshawy of Paribas said. "It's a turnaround story."
Furthermore, analysts noted that a deal to sell a stake Carso's Cigatam tobacco division to Philip Morris would not be entered into the group's books until the third quarter.
A table comparing analysts average projections for the second quarter of 1997 with the same quarter in 1996 follows:

April-June 1997 April-June 1996
Earnings per share 0.68 0.90
Sales 7.039 bln 6.392 bln
Operating earnings 1.189 bln 1.343 bln
Net earnings 625 million 823 million
*Amounts in pesos. 1996 figures restated in line with
inflation.
